# Neon as backend DB for mapstack-us — due-diligence findings

## Neon free-tier facts (as of Aug 2026)
Per Neon's own pricing/plans docs: **0.5 GB storage/project**, **100 CU-hours/project/month** compute (autoscaling up to 2 CU / 8 GB RAM), **5-minute autosuspend** to zero (cannot be disabled on Free), **5 GB/month public egress**, **100 projects/org**, **10 branches/project**, **6-hour point-in-time restore window capped at 1 GB-month** plus 1 manual snapshot, and up to 60k MAU if using Neon's bundled Auth. Hitting any limit (compute, storage, or egress) suspends compute until next billing cycle rather than silently overbilling — no surprise charges, but a hard stop. IP allowlisting is **not available on Free** (paid only), and support is community-only. Connection pooling (PgBouncer, via the `-pooler` hostname suffix) is available on Free; a 0.25 CU instance has ~97 usable pooled connections. [Neon plans docs](https://neon.com/docs/introduction/plans), [Neon pricing](https://neon.com/pricing), [connection pooling](https://neon.com/docs/connect/connection-pooling). Note: storage was cut from an earlier 3 GB/branch to today's 0.5 GB/project at some past point, while compute was doubled from 50→100 CU-hours/month in Oct 2025 post-acquisition — i.e., limits have moved in both directions historically. [GitHub discussion #6799](https://github.com/neondatabase/neon/discussions/6799)

**What forces an upgrade**: for a small OSS project, storage (0.5 GB) is the realistic first ceiling, not compute — 100 CU-hours/month with 5-min autosuspend is generous for low-traffic hobby traffic. Launch tier is usage-based, no monthly minimum: $0.106/CU-hour compute + $0.35/GB-month storage; Scale tier is $0.222/CU-hour for higher-availability compute. [Neon pricing](https://neon.com/pricing)

## Stability / ownership signal
Databricks announced acquisition of Neon for ~$1B in May 2025; Neon's own announcement said the deal would close later and that "Neon isn't going anywhere — we're doubling down," with the team staying intact, but gave no explicit free-tier commitment. [Neon/Databricks post](https://neon.com/blog/neon-and-databricks), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/05/14/databricks-is-buying-database-startup-neon-for-about-1-billion.html), [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/05/14/databricks-to-buy-open-source-database-startup-neon-for-1b/). Post-acquisition signals are actually positive for hobby users: compute price cut 15–25%, storage price cut ~80% ($1.75→$0.35/GB-mo), and free compute doubled — but a large enterprise-AI acquirer's priorities (agentic AI infra) could deprioritize a free hobby tier over a multi-year horizon; no explicit long-term free-tier guarantee found in public statements.

## Security posture
AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit; SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001/27701, HIPAA-eligible, PCI-DSS in progress; runs on AWS/Azure. [Neon security](https://neon.com/security), [Neon HIPAA post](https://neon.com/blog/hipaa). No public record of a breach found in search. Credentials are standard Postgres connection-string based (env vars), pooled via PgBouncer; IP allowlisting is a paid-tier-only feature, a real gap for a free-tier hobby deployment wanting network-level restriction.

## Open-source / lock-in verdict
The storage/compute engine (pageserver, safekeeper, compute node) is open source on GitHub (neondatabase/neon), and the separation of storage/compute is genuinely self-hostable — community control-plane projects (e.g., NeonD, Molnett's Neon Operator) exist. However, Neon's **managed control plane, billing, and cloud UX are proprietary/closed**. [neondatabase/neon](https://github.com/neondatabase/neon), [Neon Operator](https://molnett.com/blog/25-08-05-neon-operator-self-host-serverless-postgres). Practical exit risk: if the free tier disappeared, migrating off is just a standard `pg_dump`/`pg_restore` to any Postgres host — low lock-in at the data layer, moderate effort to replace Neon-specific features (branching, scale-to-zero) elsewhere.

## Alternatives (one line each)
| Vendor | Free tier (2026) | Key risk |
|---|---|---|
| **Supabase** | 500 MB DB, 1 GB file storage, 5 GB egress, 50k MAU, 2 active projects; auto-pauses after 7 days idle | [ITPathSolutions](https://www.itpathsolutions.com/supabase-free-tier-limits) — pause is manual to undo, more OSS-friendly with genuine self-host path |
| **PlanetScale** | **None** — free Hobby tier killed April 2024, cheapest plan now $5/mo | [Hobby deprecation FAQ](https://planetscale.com/docs/plans/hobby-plan-deprecation-faq) — proof vendors do cut free tiers with short notice |
| **Turso (libSQL)** | ~500 databases / 9 GB storage / 1B row reads per month (reports vary; some cite 100 DBs/5GB) | [CompareTiers](https://comparetiers.com/tools/turso) — most attractive since mapstack-us already uses SQLite client-side, letting server code reuse the same dialect, but libSQL diverges from vanilla SQLite/Postgres semantics |
| **Railway/Fly.io Postgres** | **No permanent free tier** — Railway is a 30-day/$5-credit trial then $5/mo min; Fly.io similarly trial-only ($5 credit or 2 VM-hrs/7 days) | [SaaSPricePulse Railway](https://www.saaspricepulse.com/tools/railway), [SaaSPricePulse Fly.io](https://www.saaspricepulse.com/blog/flyio-free-tier-2026) — both cut free tiers 2023-24, confirming the sector trend |

## Recommendation
Neon's free tier is a **reasonably safe bet for now**, backed by post-acquisition price cuts rather than cuts to the free tier, an open-source storage engine giving a real (if effortful) exit path, and solid compliance posture. But PlanetScale's 2024 free-tier death and Railway/Fly.io's 2023-24 cuts show this class of vendor free tier is not durable by default — budget for the Launch tier's usage-based pricing (no minimum, ~$0.35/GB-mo storage) as the realistic medium-term cost once mapstack-us adds write access, rather than assuming Free stays viable indefinitely. Supabase is the next-safest alternative if Neon's free tier is cut, given its more OSS-committed self-host story; Turso is worth prototyping given the existing SQLite affinity, but verify its query/feature parity with plain SQLite before committing.
